events.title: Victory in Europe Day
events.description: Nazi Germany's unconditional surrender, signed on May 7 and taking effect on May 8, was celebrated by the Allied nations as V-E Day. Crowds filled the streets of London, Paris, New York, and other cities, and leaders including Winston Churchill and Harry Truman announced the end of the war in Europe.
events.significance: Marked the end of World War II in Europe after nearly six years of conflict and the collapse of the Third Reich, though the war in the Pacific continued until August 1945.

events.title: Coca-Cola First Sold as a Medicine
events.description: Pharmacist John Stith Pemberton of Atlanta, Georgia, created a syrup that was first advertised and sold as a patent medicine. It was later mixed with carbonated water and marketed as a soft drink.
events.significance: The invention became the foundation of The Coca-Cola Company, one of the most recognizable brands in the world and a symbol of global consumer culture.

events.title: WHO Declares Smallpox Eradicated
events.description: The World Health Assembly officially announced that smallpox had been eradicated worldwide, following a global vaccination and surveillance campaign led by the World Health Organization. The last natural case had occurred in Somalia in 1977.
events.significance: Smallpox remains the only human infectious disease to be completely eradicated, demonstrating the power of international cooperation in public health.

events.title: Eruption of Mount Pelée
events.description: Mount Pelée on the Caribbean island of Martinique erupted, sending a pyroclastic flow that destroyed the city of Saint-Pierre. An estimated 30,000 people were killed within minutes, with only a handful of survivors.
events.significance: One of the deadliest volcanic eruptions of the 20th century, it advanced the scientific study of volcanology and pyroclastic flows.

events.title: Joan of Arc Lifts the Siege of Orléans
events.description: Joan of Arc led French forces to break the English siege of Orléans, which had lasted since October 1428. The relief of the city came just days after her arrival and the launch of French assaults on English fortifications.
events.significance: The victory turned the tide of the Hundred Years' War in France's favor and paved the way for Charles VII's coronation at Reims.
